question.text: An electric toaster has resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Ω</mi></math> at room temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>27</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>. The toaster is connected to a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> supply. If the current flowing through it reaches <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>, the temperature attained by toaster is around: (if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><none></none><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mo>∘</mo></mmultiscripts></math> )

solution.text:
Resistance at 27 °C, RT=27=60 Ω.

Final resistance, RT=2202.75=80 Ω.

Now, we can write R=R0(1+αΔT)

⇒80=601+2×10-4( T-27)

⇒T≈1694°C
